lens: code correctness, deterministic replay integrity, and Opik lifecycle auditability

findings.observation: The shipped CLI replay path ignores the profile's frozen clock, deterministic ID, and controlled timer declarations, so the same frozen control-plane scenario is not replayable as the same immutable artifact chain.
findings.evidence: evals/v2/profiles/agent-policy-replay-v1.json:43-60 declares frozen clock, deterministic IDs, and controlled timer; apps/eval-runner/src/cli.ts:207-216 and 243-252 call runEvaluationCase() without a deterministic runtime; apps/eval-runner/src/runSuite.ts:193-210 falls back to createSystemRuntimeDependencies(); apps/eval-runner/src/builtinExecutors.ts:21,446-470,579-639 and apps/eval-runner/src/modeDispatch.ts:30,99-125 stamp system time; two 2026-08-31 reruns of `pnpm --filter @talent-signal/eval-runner replay -- --id TS-TRJ-005` produced the same attemptId `attempt_076d48745e070106c4e0aa7bc2a0ea72` but different runIds, startedAt values, manifest digests (`sha256:7aae8aa36799...` vs `sha256:80d6b6118d32...`), gate digests (`sha256:8380ef264779...` vs `sha256:cd698aed27d8...`), result digests (`sha256:962445e0dbcf...` vs `sha256:c0cbfdce04f3...`), and localArtifactDigests (`sha256:34feed819db7...` vs `sha256:2578d91d91ee...`).
findings.user_impact: Digest-based release proofs, replay comparisons, and local receipts cannot be reproduced from the same frozen scenario, which weakens the platform's main claim that deterministic runs remain locally authoritative without Opik.
findings.recommendation: Thread profile-bound runtime dependencies through the real CLI and dispatcher path, remove wall-clock fallbacks for replay modes, and make replay artifact identity depend only on declared deterministic inputs rather than ambient time.
findings.verification: Run the same replay scenario twice through the production CLI path with the same frozen profile and assert identical run, manifest, gate, result, and local receipt digests, plus identical startedAt and createdAt values.

findings.observation: Opik experiment reuse is keyed only by dataset name, mode, agent definition ID, and agent definition version, so a changed agentDefinitionDigest or profileDigest under the same version label silently reuses the prior experiment identity.
findings.evidence: apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikTransport.ts:220-248 builds experimentName from datasetName, mode, agentDefinitionId, and agentDefinitionVersion, then only rejects reuse when datasetVersionId changes; no readback compares profileDigest or agentDefinitionDigest before reusing existingExperiment.id; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:36-84 proves distinct experiment IDs only for agentDefinitionVersion `1.0.0` versus `2.0.0`, not for same-version digest drift.
findings.user_impact: A prompt or policy change that keeps the same semantic version can be merged into an older Opik experiment, corrupting remote comparisons and making the experiment ledger overstate independence between runs.
findings.recommendation: Include profileDigest and agentDefinitionDigest in remote experiment identity, or hard-fail when an existing experiment name resolves to different configuration digests than the local manifest.
findings.verification: Add an Opik transport test that runs the same dataset, mode, agentDefinitionId, and agentDefinitionVersion twice with different agentDefinitionDigest or profileDigest and requires either a new experiment ID or an explicit mismatch error.

findings.observation: The Opik receipt path records the projection envelope digest as `localArtifactDigest`, which misstates the authoritative local artifact that was actually persisted before projection.
findings.evidence: packages/evaluation/src/contracts.ts:424-437 defines ProjectionReceiptV1.localArtifactDigest; packages/evaluation/src/localJsonReporter.ts:180-223 writes the true local run artifact digest into the local receipt; apps/eval-runner/src/projectionLedger.ts:144-159 maps `localArtifactDigest` to `event.envelopeDigest`; for checked-in run `evaluation_run_e5f66410-21c1-42a4-8683-118a3eaa7706`, docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-final/runs/evaluation_run_e5f66410-21c1-42a4-8683-118a3eaa7706/completion.json shows artifactDigest `sha256:c9d350aa7a0a3bfb6b5c8eca89ddab42b0d108531391d5f2ead17411ae72b3d8`, while docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/projection-ledger/opik_evaluation_run_e5f66410-21c1-42a4-8683-118a3eaa7706/0003-succeeded-f9c176d93cf0.json records envelopeDigest `sha256:2189edc525c8807293fb0a7b2e23b8a9a8404256486e3dd267c5682285d21942`.
findings.user_impact: Receipt consumers cannot reliably trace a remote Opik projection back to the immutable local artifact, so audit or cleanup tooling can bind the remote record to the wrong local object.
findings.recommendation: Pass the actual local artifact digest into the Opik completion path and persist that value in the ledger and projection receipt, or rename the contract field if the intended reference is only the export envelope.
findings.verification: Add a focused test that compares an Opik projection receipt with the local completion artifact for the same run and asserts exact equality of `localArtifactDigest`.

strengths: Oracle isolation is real: apps/eval-runner/src/modeDispatch.ts:75-97 only materializes model input and initial state for executors, while apps/eval-runner/src/deterministicEvaluator.ts:111-149 applies the repository oracle after execution.

Local-first immutability is implemented: packages/evaluation/src/localJsonReporter.ts:50-73 and 93-223 use write-once files and reject conflicting rewrites, and apps/eval-runner/src/runSuite.ts:212-245 completes the local artifact before starting optional projection.

Opik deletion and safe export have meaningful guardrails: apps/eval-runner/src/safeExportPolicy.ts:71-191 allowlists projected fields, apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikTransport.ts:177-187 pins dataset version and digest before projection, and apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikReporter.ts:204-245 verifies delete by remote readback.
missing_evidence: No checked-in test exercises deterministic behavior through the real CLI `replay` or `p0` path; the current deterministic tests inject createDeterministicRuntimeDependencies() directly in packages/evaluation/src/evaluation.test.ts:497-509 and apps/eval-runner/src/runSuite.test.ts:122-148.

No checked-in test covers same-version Opik experiment identity drift or asserts that an Opik projection receipt carries the true local artifact digest; the current Opik tests in apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikReporter.test.ts:102-172 only cover begin failure and delete readback.
vetoes: Deterministic replay is not reproducible on the shipped CLI path.
Opik experiment identity can alias distinct agent definitions that reuse the same version label.
open_questions: Should replay run IDs themselves be deterministic for frozen profiles, or should the contract introduce a separate stable replay digest that excludes operational receipt metadata?
Is reusing an agent definition version with a different digest prohibited by process, or must the transport enforce digest-level experiment separation even when version labels are reused?
